title: Garrison shift closure: annotated on-call handoff
content:
Summary:

Night garrison (22:00-06:00 PST) handoff notes. Primary focus: two small production events (latency surge on /v1/embeddings, degraded tail-latency on hosted-api chat route). No customer-facing downtime; elevated error budgets for a short window. This doc is rough — leave questions inline.

What happened (high level):
- 00:48 PST: Ops alert - 99th percentile latency for /v1/embeddings crossed 2.5s threshold across us-west-2. Alerting channel #sre-ops and paging to oncall.
- 00:55 PST: Spike correlated with a deployment that rolled a new kernel selection commit (infra PR 1245) to a subset of dedicated nodes (canary set).
- 01:04 PST: Observed increased KV-cache miss rates for long-context requests; batching efficiency fell ~30%.
- 01:10 PST: Rolled back the canary deployment; metrics returned to baseline by 01:28 PST.

Actions taken during shift:
- Rapid triage: confirmed rollback plan (Devon + Marco). Followed rollback checklist (runbook section 3.2).
- Temporary mitigations: increased short-term autoscaling headroom for embeddings pool (+2 nodes) to absorb backlog while rollback completed.
- Communication: status posted to #incident-updates at 01:12 PST, updated internal slack thread and added a brief note to the incident ticket JIRA-INC-4921.
- Post-rollback validation: ran synthetic queries (longest 16k token prefix shapes) to confirm KV-cache rebuild behavior and checked 95/99 latencies across regions.

Outstanding observations / theory:
- The new kernel selection favored a low-latency code path that reduced batching compatibility for requests with heterogeneous sequence lengths; that decreased batching density and increased per-token CPU work.
- KV-cache eviction patterns looked normal, but rebuild throughput for cold shards was slower — possible interaction between the new kernel's memory layout and our cache prefetch heuristics.
- No errors in infra logs pointing to OOM; CPU and memory remained within expected ranges. Traces show more frequent short-lived goroutine stalls during attention kernel init on rolled nodes.

Follow-ups (priority order):
1) Engineering: add a small telemetry flag to record batching density by request-shape in the canary path (owner: Marco, JIRA-ENG-3018).
2) Runtime team: schedule load-replay of the canary commit on staging with controlled heterogeneous seq-length corpus (owner: Riley).
3) SRE: augment runbook section 3.2 to include a specific rollback decision tree for kernel-level changes and add a quick command list for expanding embeddings pool (owner: Aisha).
4) Observability: create a derived metric for "effective batching utilization" and surface it in the embeddings dashboard (owner: Priya Nadar).
5) Customer comms: CS has been informed; no external alert needed. If repeated, craft a short blameless note for customers using heavy embeddings workloads.

Runbook edits to draft (notes to self):
- Section 2.1 (latency thresholds) needs explicit 99p/95p/avg thresholds per route; current doc uses only averaged SLOs — add per-route SLI examples.
- Section 3.2 (rollback): include step to snapshot KV-cache hit/miss histogram before rollback so postmortem can quantify impact.
- Add a checklist item: "When rolling kernel/quantization changes, run a micro-batching compatibility test on canary nodes for at least 30 minutes before traffic ramp."

Other items seen during shift:
- 03:32 PST: Pager for an unrelated alert — "trace-db write rate dropped" (Ticket JIRA-INC-4923). Resolved by restarting trace-ingest-job on eu-west-1; note: restart required because backpressure left queue unprocessed. Owner: Marco.
- 04:10 PST: Minor flurry of 429s from a downstream partner service; throttling resolved after partner increased capacity. Logged under linked artifacts. No action required beyond monitoring.

Tasks for incoming shift (next 06:00 PST handoff):
- Validate that the canary rollout is disabled for kernel selection and confirm flag is off for all clusters.
- Watch embeddings 99p latency for first 4 hours (graph: /dash/embeddings/latency/rolling-24h). If >1% above baseline, escalate to runtime lead.
- Check JIRA-ENG-3018 for telemetry PR and review the derived metric in staging.
- Follow up on trace-db root cause RCA; I'll leave my raw traces in the incident ticket (LINKED).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is the goroutine stall pattern reproducible on a perf machine? (Riley to try).
- Could quantization flags interact with kernel memory layout? Need runtime + research to validate.
- Should we add an automation to temporarily route long-context requests to a 'warm' pool during canary windows? Pros/cons to discuss in standup.

Useful commands / quick ops cheatsheet (copy to runbook):
- Check embeddings latency: curl -s "https://monitoring/api/metric?name=embeddings_latency&range=1h" | jq .
- Expand embeddings pool: infra-cli scale embeddings-pool --add 2 --region us-west-2
- Rollback canary: infra-cli deploy rollback --canary --change-id <change-id>

Notes to the next oncall:
- I'm handing over with the incident stabilized and rollback complete. Expect low risk but keep an eye on late rebuild effects for KV-cache over the next 2-4 hours (tail latency).
- If you see a slow re-emergence, do not immediately escalate; instead check canary flag and then run the micro-batch compatibility run (instructions in runbook draft).

Sign-off:
Aisha Thompson (garrison night lead)
- quick contact: aisha@redwood.ai (Slack: @aisha)
